dispatch: Two Arkansas ACIC families, each carrying one recorded failed obligation named ARTIFACTS from lane vf90 at base a09ef20d342929fb68141828508f38e65a5a8545, both recorded in BORDER_COHORT_REMEDIATION as EVERY_STROKE_IS_THE_FORMS_OWN_SOME_WITH_ITS_BACKGROUND_FILL_STRIPPED. Decide the stripped fills on the pixels, per widget; restore what masked printed art and leave alone what masked blank paper.

howTheSourceWasRendered.why: A removed-dark-pixel count taken against an ANNOTATION-FREE render of an AcroForm source is worthless. An AcroForm keeps much of what the court prints inside widget /AP /N appearance streams, so an annotation-free source render is missing exactly the ink whose absence from the delivered page the difference is meant to detect: both sides come up blank in the same places and the difference is zero by construction.
howTheSourceWasRendered.renderer: poppler pdftoppm 24.02.0, invoked as `pdftoppm -r 600 -gray -aa yes -f <page> -l <page> <pdf> <prefix>`. Poppler draws widget annotations and applies ISO 32000-1 12.5.5; no flag suppressing annotations was passed and none exists on this tool.
howTheSourceWasRendered.threshold: grey < 128 counts as a dark pixel, at 600 dpi, on 5100x6600 letter pages.
howTheSourceWasRendered.provedNotAssumed: The same command was run over the pinned ACIC order (b347754fd115adea52068fe5cd267f84021f8f435a7b86c02c3347dd86f9f555) and over a control copy of it with every page /Annots and the catalog /AcroForm removed. Page 1 renders 1,926,487 dark pixels normally and 1,922,979 with annotations removed. 9,622 dark pixels on that page are drawn by annotations ALONE and by nothing in page content, and the difference bounding box (x 881-1030, y 3984-4291 at 600 dpi) falls exactly on the two check-box /Rect values the source declares on that page. The render draws widget /AP /N ink, so a zero taken from it means something.
howTheSourceWasRendered.andItAlsoAnswersTheQuestion: The same control run showed 6,114 dark pixels LOST when annotations are drawn. That is the /AP /N opaque white fill covering page-content ink the form itself prints. It is the direct measurement that the stripped fills on this family masked PRINTED ART and not blank paper.
howTheSourceWasRendered.controlCopyBuiltBy: pdf-lib, page /Annots deleted and catalog /AcroForm dropped; used only as a control and never as a comparison baseline.

howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.theQuestion: Restoring a fill that covered blank paper moves bytes for nothing; leaving one that masked printed art ships a doubled frame. The two lanes that reached opposite conclusions on this class today (Colorado, Nebraska) were both right, so the answer had to be measured on these pages.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.theTest: At 600 dpi, inside each widget's own /Rect, count dark pixels three ways: the source with annotations OFF (page art alone), the source with annotations ON (what a viewer shows), and the delivered fixture.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.resultOnThisCohort: COLORADO SHAPE, not Nebraska. On the order page 1 check boxes: page art alone 3,057 dark pixels per control; source as a viewer renders it 4,811; delivered 7,868 = 4,811 + 3,057 exactly. Both drawings are present at once in the delivered page. The form prints a heavy bracketed box, the /AP covers it with `1 g 0 0 18 18 re f` and strokes its own thin 17x17 square in its place, and stripping the fill revealed the bracket while still stamping the square.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.crop: Rendered and read as an image: source page art alone is a thick bracketed box; the source as a viewer sees it is one clean thin square; the delivered page before repair carries BOTH, superimposed.
howTheStrippedFillsWereDecided.soTheRemedy: RESTORE the fill. Removing this ink would have deleted the Arkansas Crime Information Center's own check-box stroke from a petition and a proposed order.

aRTIFACTSObligationIsNotTheBorderFinding.andTheByteFinding: vf90's row names ARTIFACTS for a different reason: the delivered artifacts carried flattened widget appearances matching no pinned-source /AP /N stream byte for byte.
